status_summary: Executive Order 14303 (signed 2025-05-23) directed OSTP to issue Gold Standard Science guidance, which it published on 2025-06-23 with a 60-day agency reporting requirement; the order also requires agencies to reevaluate and revise or rescind scientific integrity policies issued between 2021-01-20 and 2025-01-20. Several agencies have since replaced or revised those policies: the Department of Energy (2025-07-24, a policy that does not cite the order), EPA (August 2025, reinstating its 2012 policy), Interior through Secretary's Order 3441 (listed 2025-08-29), Commerce (effective 2026-08-19) and the National Science Foundation (2026-09-01, a new policy that cites the order and contains no diversity, equity or inclusion terms). An EPA memorandum of 2026-04-27 implementing the order moves hazard and dose-response assessment work to the regulatory program offices; it does not separate risk assessment from risk management, and no policy doing so was found. The order's background text criticizes diversity, equity and inclusion considerations in science without an operative directive on them; the National Science Foundation began terminating such awards in April 2025.

timeline.event: The National Science Foundation began terminating awards it judged outside its priorities, including grants focused on diversity, equity and inclusion and on misinformation and disinformation.
Executive Order 14303, Restoring Gold Standard Science, was signed (published 2025-05-29).
OSTP issued agency guidance for implementing Gold Standard Science, with agencies to report publicly within 60 days.

The Department of Energy approved DOE P 411.2C, a new Scientific Integrity Policy superseding DOE P 411.2B of 2024-01-19; the policy text read does not cite Executive Order 14303 or Gold Standard Science.
EPA rescinded its January 2025 scientific integrity policy and reinstated its 2012 policy, which EPA's policy page ties to Executive Order 14303 (month-only date: August 2025).

Interior's document library lists Secretary's Order 3441, Implementing the Requirements of Executive Order 14303, under the date 2025-08-29 (the order text carries no date line and takes effect immediately). It rescinds the 2024 departmental scientific integrity chapter (305 DM 3) and Secretary's Order 3397, reinstates the 2018 open science order (SO 3369 Amendment 1), requires public release of relied-upon data and models, and gives bureaus 30 days to propose revisions to their scientific integrity policies; Interior announced it on 2025-09-04.

EPA's Deputy Administrator issued a memorandum implementing Executive Order 14303 on risk assessments: regulatory program offices are to make the science policy judgments and develop the hazard and dose-response assessments their programs need, and IRIS values are to carry a disclaimer that they are not necessarily regulatory levels. The memorandum does not use the term risk management and places assessment work in the offices that make regulatory decisions.

Commerce Department Administrative Order DAO 216-23, Scientific Integrity, took effect, replacing the 2025-01-15 version; it is issued under Executive Order 14303 and the OSTP guidance and does not expressly address political interference.

The National Science Foundation published Scientific Integrity Policy NSF.601.P (version 1.0, dated 2026-09-01), which its policy page lists as replacing NSF 24-007; the policy cites Executive Order 14303, defines inappropriate influence without an express political interference clause, and contains no diversity, equity or inclusion terms.

title: Separate risk assessment from management; unwind equity initiatives in science policy
uncertainties: Agency implementation plans were not individually reviewed. Two web searches on 2026-10-19 for litigation over the order, in addition to one earlier search, found no court case. Secretary's Order 3441 carries no date line in its text; it is dated by Interior's document library listing (2025-08-29), and Interior announced it on 2025-09-04. The NSF policy was read in its PDF form; its own supersedes field is blank while the policy page lists it as replacing NSF 24-007. An AIP news report of 2026-09-11 characterizes several agencies as removing political interference protections; that characterization was checked only where a primary policy was read (DOE, EPA, Interior, Commerce, NSF) and is not asserted. The EPA rescission date is month-only; the EPA page gives no day. The DOE policy does not cite the order, so its link to the order is timing only. The EPA risk assessment memorandum is also tracked in c13-05 and was read here only for whether it separates assessment from management; it does not. USDA, HHS and NIH policy changes were not confirmed from primary pages. EPA science is covered by c13-05 and government-wide removal of DEI terms by c00-01. The progress figure is an inference from the order, guidance and several agency policy revisions being operative while the separation element is unmet.
